article.title: Best Flooring for a Basement: How to Choose
article.summary: Choose the right basement flooring: test for moisture, check flatness, compare vinyl plank, tile, carpet tile and laminate, and plan the subfloor.
article.body:
Basements are damp, cool and built on concrete, so the floor that works upstairs can fail down here. This guide walks you through testing the slab and picking a floor that handles moisture, before you buy anything.

Safety: if the basement has a musty smell, visible mold or standing water, fix the moisture problem before any new floor goes in.

Steps

  1. Test the slab for moisture

    Tape a 2 x 2 ft square of clear plastic sheeting tightly to the bare concrete on all four sides and leave it for 24 to 72 hours. Moisture droplets under the plastic mean water is coming up through the slab; a damp top means humid air.

    Done right: you know whether the slab, the air, or neither is the moisture source.

  2. Check that the floor is flat

    Lay a 6 ft straightedge across the slab in several directions and look for gaps. Many click floors allow only about 3/16 in of variation over 10 ft; check your product's spec. Grind high spots and fill low spots with floor patch.

    Done right: the slab meets your chosen floor's flatness spec everywhere.

  3. Compare the main options

    Rigid-core vinyl plank (SPC/WPC): waterproof, warm-looking, and the most popular choice. Porcelain tile: unaffected by water and very durable, but cold and hard underfoot. Carpet tiles: warm and replaceable one square at a time if a section gets wet. Waterproof laminate: scratch-resistant but check the water rating carefully. Avoid solid hardwood below grade.

    Done right: you've narrowed it to one or two types that suit your moisture test results.

  4. Plan the underlayment and subfloor

    Follow the flooring maker's rules for concrete: most floating floors need a vapor barrier underlayment, and some include one. A raised subfloor panel system can add warmth and an air gap on a cold slab, but it raises the floor height.

    Done right: you know which underlayment the warranty requires and how much the floor height will rise.

  5. Check heights at stairs and doors

    Measure how the new floor height affects the bottom stair riser, door clearances and transitions to other rooms. Stair risers should stay within code limits, typically no more than 3/8 in difference between risers.

    Done right: doors still swing freely and the bottom step stays within code once the floor is in.

Call a waterproofing contractor if: the plastic test shows water coming through the slab, walls weep after rain, or the basement has flooded before. Fix drainage and waterproofing first, then choose the floor.

FAQ

What is the best flooring for a basement?

For most basements, rigid-core luxury vinyl plank is the best balance of waterproofing, comfort, looks and price. Porcelain tile is the most moisture-proof.

Can you put laminate flooring in a basement?

Only waterproof-rated laminate, with the vapor barrier the maker requires, and only in a basement with no water coming up through the slab.

Do I need a subfloor in my basement?

Not always. Many vinyl floors go directly over a flat, dry slab with the right underlayment. A raised subfloor adds warmth and an air gap.

How do I test my basement floor for moisture?

Tape a 2 x 2 ft piece of plastic to the slab for 24 to 72 hours. Moisture under the plastic means water is coming through the concrete.
